title: Fully learned multimodal physical control with information-preserving generic sensor encoders
question: Can a fully learned multimodal recurrent controller infer hidden motion from history and select the correct control action when generic learned sensor encoders preserve spatial and temporal sensor information?
rationale: E2E-001 was integrity-valid but failed the matched-history endpoint while achieving 0.7217 mean accuracy. The successor targets the diagnosed generic sensor-encoding bottleneck without encoding physical state, object identity, addressing rules, or task-specific computation.

arms.name: learned_data_only
arms.intervention: same fully learned multimodal recurrent controller with generic information-preserving encoders, trained only with action cross-entropy
arms.acts_on: architecture only; no privileged physical prior

arms.name: learned_physics_prior
arms.intervention: same controller and encoder with the preregistered Hamiltonian-law regularizer

held_constant: same synthetic environment and action space
same training pool and held-out evaluation generation rules
same hidden dimension and training budget as E2E-001
no hand-coded address or retrieval function
no checkpoint, seed, hyperparameter, or metric selection
architecture_change: replace global-average-pooled image encoder with learned convolutional encoder retaining a spatial feature map before projection
replace global-average-pooled audio encoder with learned convolutional encoder retaining local temporal/frequency features before projection
retain generic text encoder, multimodal fusion, recurrent temporal state, canonical latent, and direct action path
no physical state representation or object slots are introduced

allowed_information: Hamilton canonical equations dq/dt=dH/dp and dp/dt=-dH/dq
conservation of the learned Hamiltonian H on passive observation intervals
forbidden_information: masses, positions, velocities, or other physical-state labels
optimal action or target action index

leakage_rules: training and evaluation episode keys are disjoint for every seed and arm
evaluation fingerprints are distinct across seeds
both arms receive identical evaluation episodes within a seed
current audio contains speed magnitude only
goal text contains no action labels or physical-state labels
history-pair current multimodal observations are identical while correct actions differ
physics loss is computed only from model-predicted generic canonical latent trajectories

primary_end_to_end_gate.description: A positive fully learned result requires the no-prior learned model to solve held-out action selection and discriminate matched-history pairs with identical current multimodal observations.

decision_rule.condition: all integrity gates pass; learned_data_only mean accuracy >= 0.70; every learned_data_only seed >= 0.55; learned_data_only history-pair exact accuracy >= 0.70
decision_rule.licenses: bounded evidence of a fully learned end-to-end multimodal physical-control capability on the registered benchmark
decision_rule.does_not_license: real-world multimodal competence, general physical reasoning, general memory, learned semantic addressing, or scaling

decision_rule.condition: all integrity gates pass and physics-prior-minus-data-only delta >= 0.05 with bootstrap lower bound > 0
decision_rule.licenses: bounded evidence that the registered physical-law prior improves the successor model on this benchmark
decision_rule.does_not_license: a universal benefit from physics priors

decision_rule.condition: integrity passes but end-to-end gate fails
decision_rule.licenses: the successor model is not yet a demonstrated end-to-end solution on this benchmark

decision_rule.condition: any integrity or provenance gate fails

hypothesis: Generic information-preserving learned sensor encoders should improve the learned recurrent controller's ability to infer hidden motion from history; adding the preregistered Hamiltonian-law prior may provide an additional benefit without task-specific physical-state or addressing scaffolds.
